newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui group not mulling holding firm - Sakura Bank.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui group not mulling holding firm - Sakura Bank.

text.p: Sakura Bank Ltd, which is a member of the Mitsui group, said on Tuesday that the group was not considering setting up a financial holding company.

"It is not a fact that the Mitsui group is considering a holding company. And the group will not consider such an idea in the future either," Sakura president Shunsaku Hashimoto told a news conference held by the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan. He is also chairman of the federation.

Last week the president of Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co was quoted as saying by Jiji news agency that he wanted to consult financial institutions within the Mitsui group about how to deal with Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms.
Koshiro Sakata said it was possible that the group companies might set up a holding company centred on Sakura Bank, Jiji said.
Sakura's Hashimoto said the insurer apologised to the bank on Monday, adding that it was untrue that the insurer had proposed forming a holding company.

Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party and its political allies agreed last week to lift a 50-year-old ban on holding companies, enabling the government to submit a bill to parliament in March. The bill is expected to take effect early next year.
The Finance Ministry has also begun to work out guidelines and necessary revisions to financial laws to enable financial institutions to set up financial holding companies.
